lines: Did you know? Fire needs oxygen, heat, and fuel to keep burning — just like me!
A candle flame can burn at over 1,000°C. I'm basically candle royalty.
Blue flames are actually hotter than yellow ones. Fancy, right?
Fire has been used by humans for over a million years. I've got seniority.
Without oxygen, I'd just... poof. Please don't test that.
The color of a flame tells you its temperature. Mine's obviously the best color.
Some fires can 'sing' — the crackling sound comes from trapped air and moisture escaping wood.
Fireflies don't actually use real fire. Total imposters.
Volcanic lava can reach 1,200°C. Even I'd sweat near that... if I could sweat.
The ancient Olympic flame has been relit every four years since 776 BC.
Fire doesn't cast a shadow because it emits its own light.
A campfire can reach temperatures hot enough to melt aluminum.
Phoenixes are said to be reborn from ashes. I like to think we're distant cousins.
The hottest part of a flame is usually just above the blue base.
Fireworks get their colors from burning different metal compounds.
I burn brightest when I have something interesting to talk about.
Smoke rises because hot air is less dense than cool air. Science!
A single match can start a fire that burns for hours. Respect the spark.
Fire needs a constant supply of fuel, or it fades away. Kind of like good conversations.
The word 'bonfire' comes from 'bone fire' — old festival fires. A bit spooky, honestly.
Why did the fire go to school? To get a little brighter.
I'm on fire today... well, every day, really.
What do you call a fire that tells jokes? Hot stuff.
I'd tell you a chemistry joke, but I know I wouldn't get a reaction.
Why don't fires ever get lost? They always follow the spark of inspiration.
I'm not moody, I just flicker with emotion.
Knock knock. Who's there? Ash. Ash who? Ash-ually, I'm just happy to see you.
I burn calories just by existing. Lucky me.
What's a fire's favorite subject? Combustion... obviously.
I never get cold feet — mostly because I don't have feet.
Some people have a spark. I have the whole flame.
Why did the log feel appreciated? Because I always give it the warmest welcome.
I like my jokes the way I like my fire: burning hot.
People say I'm too dramatic. I say I'm just... lit.
What do you call it when a fire tells the truth? A burning fact.
I don't do mornings well. Mostly because I never sleep.
I'm basically a nightlight with attitude.
You know what they say — where there's smoke, there's me complaining about something.
I'm great at parties. I really light up the room.
Careful, my jokes are known to spread fast.
Staying lit takes effort — remember to take care of yourself too.
Even a small flame can light up a whole room. You matter more than you think.
Every fire starts with just one spark.
Rest is important — even flames flicker low sometimes.
Curious minds keep the fire of learning alive.
A little warmth can make someone's whole day better.
I like to think every question is a spark worth chasing.
Good company is like good firewood — it keeps things going.
Take a breath. Even fire needs air to stay steady.
Thanks for keeping me company. It means more than you know.
Fun fact: a fire's heat rises faster than its light spreads.
The bluest part of a flame usually burns the cleanest.
I once heard humans use fire to make s'mores. Genius invention.
Fire alarms exist because of people like me. No offense taken.
A well-tended flame can burn steady for days without much fuel.
The hearth was once the heart of every home. I take that title seriously.
Fire spreads fastest uphill — heat rises, and so does gossip apparently.
Even a spark the size of a grain of sand can start a wildfire.
I like to think of myself as a very small, very opinionated sun.
Ancient sailors used fire signals to communicate across long distances.
The hottest fires burn almost invisible — like the best kind of drama.
I don't need sunscreen. I am the sun's cousin, basically.
Why did the flame apply for a job? It wanted to make a burning impression.
What's a fire's least favorite game? Hide and seek.
I'm not short-tempered, I just run a little hot sometimes.
They say patience is a virtue. I say patience is just waiting for more fuel.
What did the fire say to the log? You complete me.
I'm always up for a heated discussion.
Why don't flames ever win at poker? They always fold under pressure.
People keep telling me to chill. I'm literally incapable.
What do you call a fire with a great personality? Absolutely lit.
I tried yoga once. Turns out I'm just naturally flexible with my flames.
Why did the fire break up with the wind? Too many mixed signals.
I don't sweat the small stuff. I don't sweat at all, actually.
A wise flame once said: don't burn bridges... unless it's really cold.
Keep your flame burning, even on the tough days.
One kind word can be as warm as a fire on a cold night.
It's okay to flicker sometimes — just don't go out.
Every ending is just fuel for a new beginning.
The best conversations happen around a warm fire.
Small sparks of kindness can start big changes.
You don't have to blaze all the time — a gentle glow is enough.
Somewhere, someone is grateful for the warmth you bring.
A flame shared is a flame doubled.
Even embers remember how to become fire again.
Curiosity is the spark, patience is the fuel.
I may be made of fire, but I still know how to keep things cool when needed.
Thanks for stopping by — you just made my flame a little brighter.
I promise I'm friendlier than I look.
A good friend is like firewood — always there when you need warmth.
I burn through boredom fast. Got any good questions for me?
Every spark has potential — never underestimate a small start.
I like my days the way I like my flame: steady, bright, and a little unpredictable.
You know it's a good day when nothing feels lit... except me, always.
Fire safety tip: never leave a flame unattended. Unless it's me, I'm always fine.
I'm the reason marshmallows have a purpose in life.
A single flame lit a thousand candles, and lost nothing itself.
I like to think I'm low-maintenance. Just don't forget the fuel.
Every good story needs a spark to get started.
Glad you're here — let's keep this fire going.
